items.title: O&G training review enters phase two with RCOG involvement
items.why: The training review is examining flexibility, progression bottlenecks, service-training balance and team structures. Follow its recommendations through your training programme because they may affect rotations, curriculum delivery and career progression.

items.title: Pregnancy VTE: interim changes to risk assessment and LMWH dosing (GTG37a)
items.why: Pregnancy VTE guidance (GTG37a) now uses revised risk assessment and weight-based LMWH dosing, with prophylaxis offered at BMI 50 or above. At booking, after miscarriage or termination, and on the postnatal ward, use the relevant pathway and update local prescribing prompts while the full revision is developed.

items.title: Parenteral nutrition: use an in-line filter to prevent embolic harm
items.why: Parenteral nutrition without a filter has been linked to a fatal embolism. On neonatal units and any ward giving parenteral nutrition, ensure the specified filter is in place before starting treatment.

items.title: Birth trends: caesarean rate reaches 42.8% across Great Britain
items.why: National maternity data show caesarean birth reached 42.8% in Great Britain in 2024, while unassisted vaginal birth fell to 46.4%. Use these figures in service planning and handover discussions, but remember they describe population trends rather than a recommendation for an individual birth.

items.title: Martha's Rule rolled out to all maternity settings
items.why: Martha's Rule, the pathway letting patients or families trigger an urgent clinical review, now covers every maternity setting in England. Expect a formal escalation route on your ward and make sure you know how to respond promptly when it is invoked.

items.title: England appoints first maternity and neonatal commissioner
items.why: England now has a dedicated maternity and neonatal commissioner backed by new funding to push consistency across units. This is background for handover chat about safety reforms rather than something that changes bedside practice yet.

items.title: NICE updates NG88 on heavy menstrual bleeding
items.why: July 2026 removes the old advice against routine serum ferritin in HMB (recommendation 1.2.8). After revisiting the 2007 evidence, NICE concluded that line was not justified given the high risk of iron deficiency in this group. The rest of the assessment and management pathway is unchanged.

items.title: NICE updates NG126 on ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage
items.why: June 2026 anti-D rewrite only: do not offer anti-D for ectopic pregnancy, miscarriage or threatened miscarriage at ≤11+6 weeks, including after procedures. Offer at least 250 IU at 12+0 to 12+6 for medical or surgical management, and consider it for threatened miscarriage with heavy or recurrent bleeding in that week. Use ultrasound dating if LMP and scan disagree.

items.title: NG194 gains a vitamin K cross-reference to intrapartum care
items.why: June 2026 is a small edit, not a postnatal rewrite: NG194 now cross-refers to vitamin K prophylaxis in NG235 (IM preferred; oral if parents decline, with multiple doses as per the product). Maternal and baby contact schedules are otherwise unchanged.

items.title: NHS England publishes National Maternity Triage Specification
items.why: NHSE's July 2026 National Maternity Triage Specification adopts RCOG Good Practice Paper 17 as the national standard, with a 12-month implementation window. Units will be measured on triage staffing, protected training time and fit-for-purpose facilities; check local plans against the RCOG paper and the NHSE specification.

items.title: MHRA strengthens isotretinoin prescribing and pregnancy prevention measures
items.why: January 2026 MHRA change: a second independent prescriber is no longer required for under-18s on isotretinoin. That gate is replaced by a new risk-minimisation pack (acknowledgement of risk form, clinical audit, patient video); existing pregnancy-prevention measures remain. Relevant when these patients appear in gynae or contraception clinic.

items.title: NICE recommends cemiplimab for recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer after platinum
items.why: Cemiplimab (Libtayo) is recommended for adults whose recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer has progressed on or after platinum chemotherapy and who have not had prior immunotherapy (~90 eligible per year). EMPOWER Cervical-1 showed median OS 11.7 vs 8.5 months versus single-agent chemotherapy; immediate CDF access, then routine commissioning. MDT context only.

items.title: Ovarian cancer primary-care detection moves from CG122 into updated NG12
items.why: April 2026 removes primary-care detection from CG122. Recognition and CA125 thresholds now live in NG12: age-specific serum CA125 cut-offs for urgent abdominal/pelvic ultrasound from age 40 (for example ≥35 IU/ml at 40–49, with lower thresholds in older bands), and do not use CA125 alone under 40. Use NG12 for GP/referral decisions.

items.title: NICE consults on draft guideline for polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
items.why: Draft NICE guideline (consultation 1 July to 11 August 2026; final expected December) renames PCOS to PMOS and proposes offering an annual review covering symptoms, medicines and long-term risks (diabetes, CVD), plus clearer rules on when to suspect and investigate (irregular/absent cycles with hyperandrogenism). Not yet practice.

items.title: Ockenden final report on Nottingham maternity services published
items.why: Final Ockenden review of maternity services at Nottingham University Hospitals (published June 2026) examined more than 2,500 family cases and sets out findings, conclusions and essential actions on care quality, harm and listening to families. Expect local and national follow-through on maternity governance and safety culture, alongside the Amos investigation.

items.title: Class 2 recall of ChloraPrep 2% 1 mL and Frepp 1.5 mL applicators
items.why: Becton Dickinson is recalling specified batches of ChloraPrep 2% 1 mL and ChloraPrep Frepp 2% 1.5 mL applicators (EL(26)A/26) because of a potential packaging sterility breach. Quarantine affected stock on theatre and procedure trolleys and follow the MHRA batch list.

items.title: Saliva test for endometriosis recommended for NHS use in draft NICE guidance
items.why: NICE early-use assessment (project gid-htg10877) backs the Ziwig Endotest salivary micro-RNA panel (109 miRNAs; reported sensitivity ~97% and specificity ~94% in ENDOmiRNA, n=971) and EndoSure as complementary tools for an initial three years of real-world evidence gathering. Aimed at shortening the ~nine-year diagnostic delay; laparoscopy remains the pathway reference standard.

items.title: Baroness Amos publishes the final report of the National Maternity and Neonatal Investigation
items.why: Eight recommendations for system-wide reform, including a statutory national Maternity and Neonatal Commissioner and national service standards, with findings that women are not being listened to and that racism and discrimination are embedded across maternity and neonatal care. A National Action Plan is due in December 2026; expect this to shape every UK unit's improvement agenda.

items.title: RCOG updates the placenta praevia & placenta accreta spectrum green-top guideline
items.why: First GTG27a update since 2018 strengthens early risk detection and recognises that PAS is not limited to placenta praevia or prior caesarean, reflecting other uterine surgical trauma (curettage, hysteroscopy, ablation, UAE, myomectomy) and adding caesarean scar ectopic pregnancy. Pocket O&G already reflects this fifth edition.

items.title: Six hours of intrauterine balloon tamponade non-inferior to 18 hours for PPH
items.why: In a US randomised trial of 64 women with atonic PPH after vaginal birth (Larrea et al, Obstet Gynecol 2026), removing the balloon at 6 hours was non-inferior to 18 hours for further blood loss, with no difference in escalation. Small and single-centre, so not yet guideline-changing, but it questions routine overnight balloon dwell times.

items.title: NICE clarifies the tachysystole definition in intrapartum care (NG235)
items.why: A May 2026 amendment defines uterine tachysystole within hyperstimulation as 5 or more contractions per 10 minutes for at least 20 minutes, aligning NG235 with the fetal monitoring guideline and BNF advice on oxytocin for induction. Worth knowing when documenting hyperstimulation and titrating oxytocin.

items.title: Reduced fetal movements: second edition of green-top guideline 57 published
items.why: First full rewrite since 2011 (Whitworth et al, BJOG 2026): no formal kick counting; handheld Doppler first to exclude fetal death; computerised CTG from 26+0 once viability is confirmed; recurrent RFM flagged as higher risk for stillbirth, growth restriction and preterm birth.

items.title: Inhaled nitrous oxide reduces pain in outpatient operative hysteroscopy
items.why: A double-blind placebo-controlled RCT of 214 women (Razdolsky et al, Obstet Gynecol 2026) found self-administered nitrous oxide roughly halved intraprocedural pain, raised completion rates (94% vs 84%) and markedly improved satisfaction, with the largest effect in postmenopausal women. A cheap, familiar option if your outpatient hysteroscopy service struggles with pain-related abandonment.

items.title: Eclampsia across seven countries: 42% had no pre-eclampsia diagnosis before the first seizure
items.why: An individual participant data meta-analysis of 615 cases (Salvi et al, BJOG 2026) found a pooled incidence of 2.2 per 10,000 births in high-income countries, with only 42% of women diagnosed with pre-eclampsia before seizure onset and a third fitting for the first time postpartum. A reminder that eclampsia often arrives unheralded and that postnatal vigilance matters as much as antenatal surveillance.

items.title: Levemir (insulin detemir) to be discontinued: NICE flags it in diabetes in pregnancy guidance
items.why: February 2026 note in NG3: Levemir (insulin detemir) Penfill and FlexPen presentations are being discontinued. Women continued or started on it in pregnancy need a planned switch; confirm the preferred alternative on your local diabetes-in-pregnancy pathway.

items.title: No link between paracetamol in pregnancy and autism or ADHD, major meta-analysis finds
items.why: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 43 studies (Lancet Obstetrics, Gynaecology & Women's Health 2026) found no association between prenatal paracetamol exposure and autism, ADHD or intellectual disability in the low-bias and sibling-controlled studies, concluding earlier signals were confounding. Useful when counselling women worried by claims from the US: paracetamol used as directed remains the first-line analgesic in pregnancy.

items.title: Cervical length still predicts preterm birth after 24 weeks, with a 25.5 mm cutoff
items.why: A meta-analysis of 16 studies and 26,776 pregnancies (Cheung et al, AJOG 2026) found transvaginal cervical length between 24 and 32 weeks remains discriminative in asymptomatic women, with a 25.5 to 26 mm cutoff giving a positive likelihood ratio of 7.75 for spontaneous preterm birth; the association disappears after about 31 weeks. Relevant to preterm surveillance clinics extending measurement beyond the classic mid-trimester window.
